items.q: Your classifier labels support tickets. On a test set it marks 40 tickets as 'refund'; 30 of those really are refunds. The set contains 50 refund tickets in total. What is the recall for 'refund'?
items.explain: Recall = true positives / all actual positives = 30 / 50 = 0.60; 0.75 (30 / 40) is the precision.

items.q: An extraction eval reports precision 0.90 and recall 0.50. What is the F1 score?
items.explain: F1 = 2PR / (P + R) = 0.90 / 1.40 = 0.64; the arithmetic mean 0.70 hides how poor the recall is.

items.q: Your pipeline returns JSON with an order_id field. Which scoring method fits the check 'is order_id correct'?
options: LLM-as-judge rating from 1 to 5
Exact match of the field against the labelled value
A human reviewer reading every output
BLEU score against the reference JSON
items.explain: When the expected answer is a single deterministic value, exact match is cheap, reproducible and strict; judges and text-similarity scores add noise for no benefit.

items.q: You are building the first eval set for a chatbot that answers HR policy questions. Which choice will hurt the eval most?
options: Keeping a held-out slice the prompt author never sees
Including the questions that failed in production last month
Writing all 50 examples yourself in one sitting from the happy path
Writing the expected answers before running the model
items.explain: An eval set made only of easy, self-written cases scores high and catches nothing; real failures, ambiguous phrasing and edge cases are what make the set useful.

items.q: CI rule: fail the build if eval pass rate drops by more than 2 points. Baseline: 184 of 200 pass. New prompt: 178 of 200 pass. What happens?
options: Passes, only 6 items changed
Fails, any drop at all fails the build
Fails, the drop is 3 points (92% to 89%)
Passes, the drop is within noise
items.explain: 184/200 = 92% and 178/200 = 89%, a 3-point regression, which exceeds the 2-point gate; the rule is applied to the rate, not the raw item count.

items.q: A trace shows one request used 1,200 input tokens and 300 output tokens. Pricing is ₹0.25 per 1,000 input tokens and ₹1.00 per 1,000 output tokens. What is the cost of the request?
items.explain: Input 1.2 x 0.25 = ₹0.30 plus output 0.3 x 1.00 = ₹0.30 gives ₹0.60; input and output tokens are priced separately.

items.q: The latency dashboard for your RAG endpoint shows p50 = 1.2 s and p95 = 6 s. What does the p95 figure mean?
options: 5% of requests take longer than 6 s
The slowest request took 6 s
The average request takes 6 s
95% of requests take exactly 6 s
items.explain: A percentile is a threshold: 95% of requests finish within 6 s and the remaining 5% are slower, which is why p95 is watched rather than the average.

items.q: A user reports a wrong answer from last Tuesday. Which logged fields let you reproduce that exact call?
options: Prompt template version, model name, and the full input including retrieved context
Only the final answer text
Server CPU usage at the time
The user's name and email
items.explain: To replay a call you need what went in and which prompt and model processed it; the output alone tells you what went wrong but not why.

items.q: You use an LLM judge to compare outputs A and B. Over 200 pairs it prefers whichever output is shown first about 80% of the time. What is the right fix?
options: Use a longer judge prompt with more criteria
Judge each pair twice with order swapped; keep consistent verdicts
Add 'be fair and unbiased' to the judge prompt
Set the judge temperature to 0
items.explain: This is position bias; swapping the order and discarding or averaging inconsistent verdicts removes it, while prompt wording and temperature do not.

items.q: An eval run has 300 items. Each item needs one generation call and one judge call, at about ₹0.60 per call. What does one full run cost?
items.explain: 300 items x 2 calls x ₹0.60 = ₹360; forgetting the judge calls halves the estimate.

items.q: Expected: 4521. Model output: "Order ID: 4521." Exact match fails although the answer is right. What is the correct fix?
options: Raise the model temperature so it varies the format
Switch the whole suite to LLM-as-judge
Mark the item as passed by hand
Normalise the output (extract the number, strip punctuation) before comparing
items.explain: Exact match should compare the normalised value being tested, not the raw string; loosening the whole suite or hand-passing items makes the eval less trustworthy.
